stories × a little machine learningMADE FOR A COFFEE BREAK.
BEHIND THE LENS

A visual starting point.
You make the final choice.

A pretrained CLIP model compares your photo with descriptions of drink families, directly in your browser. No image is uploaded to an image-recognition service. Model code and weights are downloaded from jsDelivr and Hugging Face; the first scan can take a few minutes.

It has not been trained or evaluated on Stories drink photos. It can confuse similar drinks and does not verify brands, flavors, ingredients or allergens. We show alternatives and always ask you to confirm a menu item. Low similarity triggers an uncertain result using an uncalibrated heuristic.

The optional reference-photo mode uses the same pretrained vision encoder to compare your image with a separate, openly licensed example gallery. These are outside photos, not verified Stories products. Cosine similarity measures appearance, not correctness. The gallery and mapping are separate files; the original transaction CSV is unchanged. Description mode does not load or require the gallery. Add ?references=off to the URL to hide it entirely.

Pairings come from aggregate January–May transaction data. We use a simple drink/branch co-purchase rule, weighted by branch-specific margin. This is a product-level extension of the baseline, not our category XGBoost model. It has no measured recommendation uplift. No purchase or order is placed here.

The optional test log contains only this session’s suggested families, confirmed menu selections, timing and pairing clicks. It stays in memory until you download it or leave. No images or customer identifiers are included. Test selections are not purchases and are not used to retrain the model.
